records.applies_when: A State contract incorporates the Cloud Hosting Appendix V.26.1. The vendor submits independent audit evidence.
records.summary: Provide current assurance at award and annually, with applicable bridge letters. The State prefers SOC 2 Type 2 and may accept comparable evidence if unavailable. Participate in third-party risk review at onboarding and on request.

records.applies_when: A State contract incorporates the Cloud Hosting Appendix V.26.1. State data is stored or transmitted.
records.summary: Document AES encryption with at least 256-bit keys under current FIPS 140 controls. Give the State interoperable control of keys for data at rest.

records.applies_when: A State contract incorporates the Cloud Hosting Appendix V.26.1. A vendor proposes a secondary use of State data.
records.summary: Limit use to contract purposes. Replication to nonproduction requires prior written authorization. Training or fine-tuning AI or machine learning with State data is prohibited even after anonymization or aggregation.

records.applies_when: A State contract incorporates the Cloud Hosting Appendix V.26.1. The State requests its data or the contract ends.
records.summary: Deliver a current, complete machine-readable export in a nonproprietary format preserving metadata and integrity. Assist secure exit migration at no extra cost.

records.applies_when: A State contract incorporates the Cloud Hosting Appendix V.26.1. The hosted service requires credentials for user or administrative access.
records.summary: Support State identity federation, enforce MFA on privileged accounts, and obtain written State authorization before maintaining local accounts for State personnel.

records.applies_when: A State contract incorporates the Cloud Hosting Appendix V.26.1. The State requests system logs.
records.summary: Log the Appendix S1 events throughout the contract and deliver requested logs within 24 hours. Retention follows enterprise policies and applicable law.

records.applies_when: An entity handling nonpublic personal data, including a government agency, assesses an incident under the Illinois Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA).
records.summary: Section 5 defines breach as unauthorized acquisition of computerized data compromising personal information. Its two personal-information tests cover specified identifiers paired with a name, or online account access credentials, subject to encryption, redaction and key-compromise qualifications.
records.locator: 815 ILCS 530/5, definitions of data collector, breach and personal information

records.applies_when: A collector discovers or is informed of a statutory breach of personal information it owns or licenses concerning an Illinois resident.
records.summary: Notify affected residents free of charge as promptly as possible, accounting for scoping and restoration. A written law-enforcement request can delay notice until it no longer interferes with the investigation.

records.applies_when: A maintainer or storage provider discovers unauthorized acquisition, or reasonably believes it occurred, involving computerized personal data owned or licensed by another party.
records.summary: Immediately notify the owner or licensee and cooperate with the owner’s investigation and notification work as specified in the statute.

records.applies_when: One breach requires a collector to notify more than 500 Illinois residents under §10, and the §50 exception does not apply.
records.summary: Notify the Attorney General promptly and by the time consumers receive notice. If the breach date is unknown, forward it once determined.

records.applies_when: A state agency collecting an Illinois resident’s personal information discovers or receives notice of a breach of system data or written material.
records.summary: Notify the resident at no cost promptly, subject to scoping, restoration and a qualifying written law-enforcement delay. Written material is expressly covered.

records.applies_when: A single state-agency breach concerns personal information of more than 250 Illinois residents.
records.summary: Notify the Attorney General by the earlier of resident notification or 45 days after discovery, subject to the specified good-cause and written law-enforcement exceptions.

records.applies_when: An agency directly responsible to the Governor experiences or reasonably suspects a single breach affecting more than 250 Illinois residents’ personal information or an instance of aggravated computer tampering.
records.summary: Notify both the DoIT Chief Information Security Officer’s office and the Attorney General without delay, within 72 hours of discovery.

records.applies_when: A state agency collecting personal data discovers or learns of a breach affecting system data or written material.
records.summary: Report to the General Assembly within five business days, describing breaches and corrective measures. Agencies that file must also report annually.

records.applies_when: A state agency determines the identity of the actor responsible for its breach.
records.summary: Report the identity to the General Assembly within five days of determination if doing so preserves residents’ security and the investigation.

records.applies_when: A data collector maintains an Illinois resident’s personal information or contracts to disclose that information.
records.summary: Apply reasonable security measures to the records. The disclosure contract must require comparable safeguards from the recipient. Section 45 also identifies deemed-compliance provisions.

records.applies_when: A HIPAA covered entity or business associate complies with the federal privacy and security standards in §50 and owes breach notice to the U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services.
records.summary: For deemed PIPA compliance, provide the same notice to the Illinois Attorney General within five business days of notifying the Secretary.

records.applies_when: An organization needs to submit breach notice to the Illinois Attorney General.
records.summary: The Attorney General publishes the OAG Data Breach Notice System, a separate inquiry contact and a list of information to include.
records.locator: Data Breach Reporting for Businesses and State Government Agencies

records.applies_when: A person works for an Illinois county or municipality.
records.summary: Complete cybersecurity training annually, covering phishing detection, spyware and identity-theft prevention, and breach prevention and response. The employer can use the state program or develop its own.

records.applies_when: The jurisdiction is a county or is a municipality with at least 35,000 residents.
records.summary: The chief executive or delegate designates a local official or employee as the cybersecurity contact and reports current contact details to the Statewide CISO.

records.applies_when: An Illinois local officer or agency proposes disposing of a public record.
records.summary: Obtain prior written approval from the appropriate Local Records Commission unless law provides otherwise. The retention period and authority to dispose must both be checked.

records.applies_when: A local agency subject to the Downstate or Cook County rules plans routine disposal of scheduled records.
records.summary: File the disposal certificate with the appropriate commission 30 days before destruction. Wait for its approved return and retain the duplicate. The rule covers electronic and paper records.

records.applies_when: A local public or nonpublic record concerns a police misconduct complaint, investigation or adjudication.
records.summary: Retain these records permanently. The Local Records Act prohibits their destruction.

records.applies_when: An Illinois LEADS agency retains its monthly criminal history record information (CHRI) log.
records.summary: The minimum is one year, rising to three years if the monthly log doubles as the secondary dissemination log. ISP describes online availability of at least 18 months.

records.applies_when: A LEADS agency documents record validations.
records.summary: Preserve validation packets with each listed record’s status for at least 18 months.

records.applies_when: A LEADS agency manages computerized hot file entries, modifications and add-ons.
records.summary: Retain acknowledgments while active. For cleared, cancelled or purged files, keep the supporting copies and clearance evidence at least one year from clearance.
records.locator: p. 1, Active CHF, Active Add-ons and Cleared CHF

records.applies_when: A LEADS agency retains documentation of a valid hit.
records.summary: The seven-year category includes missing or wanted persons, guns, plates and stolen or felony vehicles. The one-year category includes protection orders, sex offenders and supervised release. Consult the schedule for the complete file lists.

records.applies_when: An Illinois LEADS agency retains messages, bulletins and agreements.
records.summary: Keep directed messages and daily bulletins for at least one year. Keep agreements until either agency terminates them and ensure the current agency head has signed.
records.locator: p. 1, Directed Messages, Daily Bulletin and LEADS Agreements

records.applies_when: A member of the public requests Illinois conviction information.
records.summary: The public can obtain conviction information that Illinois law requires ISP to collect and maintain, subject to statutory restrictions on its use or disclosure.

records.applies_when: A requester needs to know which events qualify as conviction information.
records.summary: A judgment of guilt or nolo contendere can include its related arrest, charges, sentence and release history. A reversal or vacatur of the guilty judgment removes its status as conviction information.

records.applies_when: A requester uses UCIA for employment or licensing.
records.summary: Retain the individual's signed release for at least two years and give them ISP's response. The individual has seven working days after receiving their copy to notify the requester of inaccurate or incomplete information.

records.applies_when: An organization submits UCIA requests in an automated format.
records.summary: Sign ISP's user agreement, follow its transmission specifications and include the subject's name, race, sex and date of birth along with the requester's complete response address.

records.applies_when: A requester uses identifying information without fingerprints under the circumstances permitted in § 11(A).
records.summary: ISP warns that identity is uncertain. When identifiers match multiple individuals, ISP withholds results except in the statutory exigency or criminal-law circumstances and may request additional identifiers or fingerprints.

records.applies_when: ISP releases conviction information outside the agency under UCIA.
records.summary: ISP keeps each dissemination record for at least three years, including the subject, requester, recipient address and dates. The subject may request the records for the listed public, private and noncriminal-justice requests.

records.applies_when: ISP verifies an error or receives an updated conviction disposition after responding to a requester.
records.summary: ISP corrects verified inaccuracies or omissions. When a subsequent conviction disposition or change is reported within 30 days of the response, ISP notifies the requester. Other Illinois law may require a longer notification period.

records.applies_when: A requester wants to pass along an ISP UCIA result or continue relying on its accuracy.
records.summary: Unless another law permits it or exigency applies, the requester has 30 days after receipt for further dissemination. Afterward a fresh request is required to redistribute the information or rely on its accuracy and completeness.

records.applies_when: A noncriminal-justice agency, commission or member of the public seeks an ordinary background check.
records.summary: Route ordinary noncriminal requests to BOI. CHIRP handles name-based requests. Do not query LEADS or pass LEADS histories to these recipients. For a listed statutory use, follow its specific process, including the limited public-housing acknowledgment.

records.applies_when: A state agency or local governmental unit covered by § 3(B) seeks conviction information about staff, prospective staff or license applicants.
records.summary: On written application and payment, covered bodies can submit fingerprints to ISP for state and FBI conviction checks. ISP sends the prints to the FBI. This particular authorization excludes school districts.

records.applies_when: An applicant needs a fingerprint-based background check for licensing or statutorily required employment.
records.summary: Obtain the correct information from the sponsoring agency before visiting a licensed live scan vendor. Out-of-state applicants use a vendor listed for card scan. ISP identifies its separate out-of-state request form as UCIA-only.
records.locator: Illinois and out-of-state fingerprint background check instructions

records.applies_when: A person applies for an individual fingerprint vendor license.
records.summary: Applicants document completion of ISP-conducted or authorized vendor training and submit fingerprints for checks against Illinois and FBI criminal history databases. The statute lists additional license qualifications.

records.applies_when: A fingerprint vendor agency applies for or maintains its license.
records.summary: Submit ISP certification that the fingerprint equipment and software meet state specifications. Continued compliance is a licensing condition. Section 31-10(a)(14) addresses individual vendors exempt from an agency license.

records.applies_when: A licensed fingerprint vendor provides a fingerprint service.
records.summary: Document the location, date, customer identifiers and signature, routing and provider identifiers on the work order. Retain it for two years from service and make it available to the licensing department or ISP for inspection.

records.applies_when: A local law-enforcement agency provides criminal-justice or noncriminal-justice fingerprinting services.
records.summary: The statute exempts local officers performing criminal-justice duties under § 31-5(a). It separately exempts members acting for a local agency registered with ISP for noncriminal-justice fingerprinting. The specified reasonable fees are permitted.

records.applies_when: An individual requests access to their own Illinois criminal history.
records.summary: After confirming that the record concerns the requester, ISP must release whether a record exists and provide a process to review and correct it. Statutory disclosure exceptions govern release to others.

records.applies_when: An individual requests their own transcript through an Illinois law-enforcement or correctional facility or licensed fingerprint provider.
records.summary: The provider forwards fingerprints and identifiers to ISP within five days of the request. After receiving a standards-compliant submission, ISP sends a transcript or no-record statement within seven days for electronic prints or 45 days for a fingerprint card.

records.applies_when: The subject elects facility delivery of their personal Access and Review result.
records.summary: The facility has two days after receipt to notify the subject, releases the document only to the subject and destroys it if unclaimed 45 days after notification. A subject may alternatively designate their residence.

records.applies_when: An individual obtains fingerprints for their personal record review or challenge.
records.summary: The collecting facility or licensed provider may waive its fee or charge up to its actual cost. ISP charges no processing fee for Access and Review or Record Challenge submissions.
records.locator: 20 Ill. Adm. Code § 1210.30 and ISP Access and Review fee guidance

records.applies_when: An individual disputes the accuracy of their ISP criminal history transcript.
records.summary: Submit a written explanation to ISP. ISP provides a written determination through the Record Challenge process. An individual dissatisfied with the response may pursue administrative appeal under 20 Ill. Adm. Code Part 1510.
records.locator: 20 Ill. Adm. Code § 1210.40(a)–(b) and ISP Record Challenge instructions

records.applies_when: Illinois police arrest a person for a reportable state offense.
records.summary: Report covered felonies and Class A or B misdemeanors daily, with the specified identifiers and fingerprints. Section 5 excludes most traffic offenses and Class B conservation offenses. It gives separate age and offense rules for minors.

records.applies_when: Police arrest a minor for an offense that would be a felony if committed by an adult.
records.summary: Daily reporting covers minors aged ten or older for these arrests. Juvenile Class A or B misdemeanor fingerprints may be forwarded to ISP. The section places separate age-, offense- and adult-transfer limits on forwarding records to the FBI.
records.locator: 20 ILCS 2630/5, juvenile collection and federal forwarding

records.applies_when: A reportable arrest occurs, or a prosecutor charges or declines a case reported to ISP.
records.summary: Arresting agencies send fingerprints, charges and descriptions daily and notify ISP of decisions against referral. The state's attorney reports filed and added charges, delinquency petitions and decisions against charging reported arrests. The default event-reporting window is 30 days unless specified otherwise.
records.locator: 20 ILCS 2630/2.1, introductory paragraph and (a)–(b), P.A. 104-692 version

records.applies_when: The circuit court disposes of a charge in a case for which ISP received the covered arrest or fingerprint information.
records.summary: The clerk reports dispositions by charge, including acquittals, convictions and sentences, dismissals, and specified later orders. The default reporting period is 30 days from the event. The Supreme Court prescribes the form and manner.
records.locator: 20 ILCS 2630/2.1, introductory paragraph and (c), P.A. 104-692 version

records.applies_when: ISP identifies incomplete, missing or incorrect arrest, charge or disposition data from an entity required to report under § 2.1 or § 5.
records.summary: Respond within 30 days unless record volume makes that impracticable. Supply the missing information or correction, or explain why it cannot be supplied and estimate when the entity can comply.

records.applies_when: A recipient seeks access to information reported to ISP under the Criminal Identification Act.
records.summary: Treat reported information as confidential. Disclosure requires express permission under state or federal law.

records.applies_when: Beginning January 1, 2027, a statutory pretrial services agency seeks to transmit arrest information.
records.summary: With ISP approval, a qualifying pretrial services agency may submit fingerprints, charges and descriptions in the same manner as an arresting agency under subsection (a).

records.applies_when: A requester seeks law-enforcement or municipal ordinance records of someone investigated, arrested or taken into custody before age 18.
records.summary: Unexpunged juvenile law-enforcement records are confidential. Apply the statutory recipient, purpose and court-order conditions. The statute identifies the minor, parents, guardian and counsel, and permits law-enforcement access for specified official duties.

records.applies_when: An agency reviews juvenile law-enforcement records of events before age 18 for annual automatic expungement.
records.summary: By January 1 each year, expunge entries meeting the statutory one-year elapsed, no charges or petition, and six-month no-subsequent-arrest-or-filing tests. Apply the separate verification rule and five-year rule for statewide student confidential reporting submissions.

records.applies_when: An agency implements an Illinois expungement or sealing order.
records.summary: Expungement calls for destruction or return and index removal, subject to the circuit-court file impoundment provision. Sealing retains the records with restricted access. Subsection (K) distinguishes sealing under the automatic process in subsection (k).
records.program: Illinois Criminal Identification Act record relief

records.applies_when: Beginning January 1, 2028, a clerk reviews municipal ordinance and Class C misdemeanor cases for statutory sealing.
records.summary: Every January 1 and July 1 the clerk seals the covered records without petition once a year has elapsed since case closure as designated by the Supreme Court.
records.program: Illinois Criminal Identification Act record relief

records.applies_when: Beginning January 1, 2029, an eligible adult or adult-prosecution record created on or after January 1, 1970 reaches the statutory sealing schedule.
records.summary: Subject to the specified appropriations, ISP identifies and seals eligible records and notifies clerks electronically. The law specifies quarterly processing for covered (k)(5) records and phased deadlines for older records. Eligibility and waiting periods depend on the record.
records.program: Illinois Criminal Identification Act record relief

records.applies_when: A public housing authority requests an adult applicant or tenant check for screening, lease enforcement or eviction.
records.summary: Local criminal-justice agencies may perform the designated housing inquiry. Tell the authority only whether a record is possible or no record was found. The full history and other LEADS/NCIC information cannot be provided.
records.program: Public housing authority checks through LEADS

records.applies_when: A city, village or town seeks background checks for its employees or liquor license applicants.
records.summary: ISP directs these checks to BOI as fingerprint-based noncriminal-justice submissions under the assigned noncriminal-justice agency identifier. Using LEADS for those employment or licensing checks is prohibited.

records.applies_when: A law-enforcement agency that maintains a tow rotation list elects to require owner or operator background checks.
records.summary: The agency can request state and FBI fingerprint checks through BOI. Obtain a noncriminal-justice agency identifier, sign the noncriminal-justice user agreement and register for the secure results portal. A criminal-justice identifier and LEADS are prohibited for this purpose.

records.applies_when: An agency submits applicant fingerprints for criminal-justice employment.
records.summary: Give the applicant the written FBI Privacy Act statement and written procedures for reviewing and amending Illinois and FBI III history. The bulletin separately specifies signed fingerprint consent and notification for submissions covered by the named concealed-carry MOU.

records.applies_when: An agency configures records software to classify adult and juvenile reportable offenses.
records.summary: BOI publishes a fixed-width statute table with offense and reporting indicators. The public page displays March 5, 2025 as its file version and describes a quarterly update cycle. Check the file version and current law when using it.
records.locator: Criminal Justice Statutes, file description and layout

records.applies_when: A requester estimates ISP charges for an applicant check, public UCIA request or their own record review.
records.summary: ISP lists $30 for the combined state/FBI electronic fee-applicant check, $10 for a UCIA electronic name inquiry and $15 for a UCIA electronic fingerprint inquiry. ISP charges no fee for personal Access and Review or Record Challenge.
records.locator: Fee Applicants, UCIA Requests and Access and Review rows

records.applies_when: A state or local law enforcement agency considers direct database access for ICE, CBP or another federal entity enforcing civil immigration violations.
records.summary: Absent a federal criminal warrant or a requirement of federal law, agencies may neither provide direct access to a law enforcement database or data-sharing platform nor enter into or maintain an agreement for it. The Act preserves cooperation on criminal investigations.
records.locator: 5 ILCS 805/15(h)(4)–(5), (i) and Attorney General guidance, p. 4

records.applies_when: An immigration agent asks a law enforcement agency for information about someone in custody or for nonpublic release or contact details.
records.summary: Section 15(h) restricts answers to custody inquiries and disclosure of nonpublic release or contact details, subject to its federal criminal warrant and federal law exceptions. Section 5 separately preserves specified exchanges about citizenship or immigration status.
records.locator: 5 ILCS 805/15(h)(6)–(7) and 5 ILCS 805/5. See Attorney General guidance, p. 4 and note 15 on public information.

records.applies_when: An officer receives an NCIC or LEADS notification and needs to establish the character of the record.
records.summary: The Act permits contacting another law enforcement agency to clarify whether a notification or other NCIC or LEADS record is civil or criminal. Section 15(i) preserves cooperation on criminal investigations, including investigations conducted by Homeland Security Investigations.

records.applies_when: An ISP auditor assigns a state CJIS audit to an agency.
records.summary: After ISP contacts the agency, use CJIS Audit on the Illinois CJIS Launchpad to submit the assigned audit, respond to findings and view the final report. The publicly linked previews are preparation aids. The auditor issues the agency credentials.
records.locator: CJIS Audits introduction and linked Using CJIS Audit v. 2.0, p. 1

records.applies_when: An agency prepares evidence for a LEADS CHRI usage audit.
records.summary: The public example asks the agency to identify each inquiry selected by the auditor, give its specific purpose and any associated case or warrant number, and identify any secondary recipient by agency name and identifier. Confirm the questions against the agency's actual assignment.
records.locator: LEADS CHRI Usage Audit, CHRI section, pp. 1–3, printed July 25, 2018

records.applies_when: A reviewer needs the documented status of Illinois under the National Crime Prevention and Privacy Compact as of July 2025.
records.summary: The FBI grouped Illinois with the states and territories that signed a memorandum of understanding with the Compact Council. The map lists ratifying Compact states separately.
records.locator: July 2025 map, Illinois (IL) and red MOU legend
records.program: National Crime Prevention and Privacy Compact

records.applies_when: A contractual employee has access to CJI while working for ISP.
records.summary: The ISP supervisor obtains and keeps a signed FBI Security Addendum on ISP form 2-683 and verifies the appropriate security awareness certification. Supervisors cover physical or logical and direct or indirect access in their training review.

records.applies_when: An ISP supervisor authorizes access to a CJI system.
records.summary: Limit access to what the job requires. The supervisor contacts the authorizing entity for that system to grant, change or remove access.

records.applies_when: An ISP user proposes connecting a personally owned device to a system containing CJI.
records.summary: Evaluate operational need, security and access requirements case by case under the applicable FBI controls.

records.applies_when: ISP personnel use a public AI system from any device.
records.summary: ISP prohibits entering CJI, LEADS information or personal information. The directive also prohibits text-based AI for law-enforcement report drafting.

records.applies_when: An AI application is to be installed on department-issued devices or an official work product uses AI.
records.summary: Installation requires approval by DoIT, the ISP Legal Office and Division of Justice Services. Official work using AI requires human review and validation. Published ISP documents produced with generative AI require a disclosure.

records.applies_when: An ALPR user would sell, share, transfer or allow access to ALPR information to a state or local jurisdiction.
records.summary: Illinois prohibits those transfers for investigating or enforcing laws interfering with covered lawful health care or permitting detention or investigation based on immigration status. The definition includes privately operated readers to the extent data is shared with law enforcement.

records.applies_when: An Illinois ALPR user proposes sharing ALPR information with out-of-state law enforcement.
records.summary: First obtain the receiving agency’s written affirmation that its use will comply with subsection (b). Withhold sharing if the declaration has not been executed.

records.applies_when: Using images from cameras in the Expressway Camera Act program.
records.summary: Authorized investigations include motor vehicle theft and forcible felonies. The statute bars use to enforce petty or unlisted offenses unless images relate to expressway or highway safety or hazards. It also prohibits discriminatory monitoring.

records.applies_when: An image from an Expressway Camera Act camera is exported through a law-enforcement database.
records.summary: Delete the exported image from that database within 120 days unless relevant to an ongoing investigation or pending criminal trial.

records.applies_when: ISP, IDOT and the Toll Highway Authority report to the General Assembly on the camera program.
records.summary: A joint annual report is due August 1 and covers county costs and investigative use. ISP’s FY26 submission was dated July 27, 2026.

records.applies_when: ISP stores ALPR records in VehicleManager or FlockOS.
records.summary: VehicleManager retains detections for 90 days and preserves search and hit/alert records permanently. FlockOS purges detections every 30 days.

records.applies_when: ISP personnel use the department ALPR systems.
records.summary: The statewide coordinator conducts monthly audits. Users enter a valid case number and an authorized search purpose when the ALPR system prompts them.

records.applies_when: Researching enforcement of restrictions on sharing Illinois ALPR data.
records.summary: The Secretary of State reported that its sample covering 12 local agencies identified federal Customs and Border Protection access to Illinois Flock cameras and that it ordered Flock to stop that access.

records.applies_when: Naperville Police stores an ordinary plate read.
records.summary: Purge routine reads after 30 days. Retain data with actual or reasonably anticipated evidentiary value, subject to a preservation duty or otherwise required by law or department policy.

records.applies_when: Naperville audits access to its plate-reader system.
records.summary: Document a monthly audit of a representative sample of searches and review unusual activity indicators where available. Stored data access must support recording user identity, date, time and activity.

records.applies_when: A vendor supplies Naperville’s plate-reader technology.
records.summary: The department requires safeguards for its data and compliance with applicable CJIS requirements, the contract and department policy. The order subjects transmission and storage to applicable LEADS and CJIS requirements.

records.applies_when: The parties to DuPage’s Revize contract sign a written agreement or amendment making a CJI-handling service an explicit deliverable.
records.summary: Section 10 imposes CJI obligations. The exhibit also requires prior written vendor approval for intentional county upload or transmission of CJI. The board approved the underlying CMS and hosting contract on April 14, 2026.

records.applies_when: The parties to DuPage’s Revize contract sign a written agreement or amendment making a CJI-handling service an explicit deliverable.
records.summary: Section 10 requires signed addenda before CJI access, including relevant subcontractors, and state and national fingerprint checks adjudicated by the county or its delegate before access. The exhibit gives six months from assignment for initial awareness training. For LEADS access, ISP requires training before access.

records.applies_when: The parties to DuPage’s Revize contract sign a written agreement or amendment making a CJI-handling service an explicit deliverable. The solution uses cloud infrastructure for CJI.
records.summary: The cloud provider must meet CJIS requirements and have a signed addendum. The county reserves the right to approve or reject that cloud provider.

records.applies_when: The parties to DuPage’s Revize contract sign a written agreement or amendment making a CJI-handling service an explicit deliverable. A security incident involves or potentially involves CJI.
records.summary: Report to both the county CIO and Illinois State Police CJIS Systems Officer within one hour of discovery.

records.applies_when: An Illinois law enforcement agency or its camera vendor retains recordings subject to the Officer-Worn Body Camera Act.
records.summary: Keep recordings 90 days, then destroy unflagged recordings subject to the supervisor-designated training exception. Early alteration, erasure or destruction is prohibited except for a non-law-enforcement activity or encounter. Document any early alteration, erasure or destruction, including actor and reason, for one year.

records.applies_when: A covered body-camera encounter is flagged, including when a complaint or covered use of force occurs.
records.summary: Protect the recording against alteration or destruction for two years from flagging. If used in criminal, civil or administrative proceedings, destruction requires both final disposition and a court order.

records.applies_when: A contractor, subcontractor or agent works for an Illinois state agency or unit of local government.
records.summary: BIPA §25(e) excludes the entity while performing that government work. Establish the relationship and the specific work covered. CJI access and screening have their own sources of authority.

coverage_gaps.detail: The AlaCOP manuals portal requires an agency login. Only its public landing page was reviewed.

ALEA describes its audit program. A currently applicable Alabama notice identifying the FBI edition used for a specific audit and any transition window was not located in the public materials reviewed.
OIT publishes requirements for State systems. A statewide CJIS hosting, data-residency or authorization rule covering every county or municipal agency was not established by this review.
OIT publishes a route for state systems. A statewide CJI-specific operational incident form, recipient or deadline for all local agencies was not located in the public ALEA materials reviewed.

The LPR rule names a vendor agreement, and an individual city authorized one. The current blank ALEA agreement, a generally applicable screening packet or list of preapproved vendors was not verified.
The published 48-hour rule depends on establishment of the State LPR Registry. The rule and materials reviewed do not confirm its operational start date.
Section 41-9-650.4 authorizes Rap Back. A current ALEA announcement of general enrollment, service start date and participant instructions was not verified.
Commission ABC appendices describe legacy employer and third-party arrangements. Current ALEA instructions applying those arrangements to downstream disclosures under §41-9-650.1(f) were not located.
DPS publishes the 5.9.5 audit cutoff and 6.1 readiness guidance. Its documents index does not name a binding audit baseline for dates after March 31, 2027.

OCA’s live PSRS training table specifies annual security awareness for all users and biennial mobile-access certification for users who run queries. Its May 11 PDF mixes annual language with biennial awareness instructions. Use the live table and confirm unusual roles with the agency terminal coordinator.

The state supplement specifies the deployment environment and offshore cleartext condition. A particular service’s authorization boundary, support access and the customer's signed acceptance must be established for that deployment.

ISP links FBI v6.1 and an older LEADS v2.2 PDF with conflicting dates. A statewide audit cutover date and the edition assigned to a particular audit were not established by these public materials. Verify with the assigned ISP auditor.

The undated FAQ describes ISP’s approach to implementation review. Obtain the agency’s accepted solution scope, key access, subcontractor and administrator screening, and current applicable control evidence for the actual deployment.

The LEADS form identifies the CSA ISO and the local reporting workflow. The form gives no numerical deadline for LASO-to-CSA notice. FBI v6.1 IR-6(a) separately requires personnel to notify the organizational incident-response function immediately and within one hour of discovering a suspected incident. Verify the state or agreement timetable for onward reporting.

ISP’s LEADS FAQ addresses U.S. storage and transmission. The State cloud appendix applies when incorporated into a contract. Public evidence reviewed does not establish a named cloud authorization such as FedRAMP for every Illinois local agency.
The actual questionnaire, assignment-specific edition, responses, findings and final report are provided within the agency's auditor-assigned account. ISP's July 2018 CHRI form is a public preview.

The DuPage Revize exhibit makes section 10 conditional on a signed CJI deliverable. The public board award establishes CMS and hosting approval. Verify a signed agreement covering CJI before applying this clause to an actual system.
